globalRules: Assume Haitian Creole Foundations or equivalent prerequisite knowledge.
Previously learned Course 1 language may be reused as context but must not become the primary teaching target.
Introduce only the grammar or vocabulary needed for the current communicative task.
Use official Kreyòl spelling and preserve meaningful diacritics as supported by the supplied source documents.
Use integrated receptive and productive practice where it helps the concept; do not force a fixed exercise rhythm.
Do not use programming runtime or code-workspace language.
Do not describe speech transcript matching as a pronunciation score.
Do not grade the Week 2 plim definite-article form while the supplied source contains both plim nan and plim lan.
Module 1 must have accessOverride free; later modules inherit paid access.

notes: Course 1 already taught that a definite marker follows the noun; do not reteach that as the module objective.
Use the Week 2 article rules and examples, excluding disputed plim grading.
Course 1 already used basic pronouns and possessor-after-noun phrases.
Do not rebuild the Course 1 basic question module.
Use the new question forms in functional health exchanges.
Treat simple present and present-progressive ap as known.
Add past and future through familiar action sentences.
Treat basic se identity as known from Course 1.
Do not require memorization of the entire Week 7 adjective table at once.
